key_insight: A thin LAGP coating on a polyethylene separator can reduce polysulfide shuttle in thin Li-S batteries while preserving the separator’s flexibility.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical separator-coating route to improve Li-S battery durability without replacing polymer separators with brittle ceramics.
method: Ion-sputtered LAGP nanofilms were deposited on polyethylene separators.
Some coatings were further modified with Ni and Co ferroic elements.
SEM and staircase voltammetry were used to assess morphology and electrochemical behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that LAGP-coated PE separators significantly influenced polysulfide diffusion and suppressed shuttle-related processes in Li-S batteries.
watch_item: The ceramic coating may still pose integration challenges for flexible devices, especially if uniform thin-film coverage or mechanical robustness is insufficient.
paper_title: Study of LAGP coating on polyethylene separator for polysulfide suppression in thin Li-S batteries
